state.conflict: Error: IP clashes with a device

traps.title: Services
traps.description: Which services the Trap IPs answer on. Each Trap IP answers only the services picked for it; its other ports are closed, as on a real machine. A trap records what its service can see, listed under each service. A bare TCP connect that sends nothing is not recorded for SMB or MSSQL.
traps.caption: Services and their status
traps.noTrapIp: None. Add this service to a Trap IP to open it.
traps.testOffReason: No Trap IP that is on has this service. Add it to a Trap IP first.
traps.testToast: Recorded a test hit on the {{service}} trap
traps.testNote: Test a trap to confirm it records hits. The test comes from the Vedette box itself, is labelled as a test, is not counted as a hit and sends no alert.
traps.testConflictReason: Every Trap IP with this service clashes with a real device. Change its address before testing.
traps.limitsTitle: One box, one share name and one login page
traps.smbName: Every Trap IP with SMB shows the same file share under the NetBIOS name {{name}}: the name of the first Trap IP with SMB. The other names are labels Vedette uses in alerts.
traps.smbNone: No Trap IP that is on has SMB.
traps.httpPage: Every Trap IP with HTTP shows the same {{page}}. It is the NAS login page when the first Trap IP with HTTP looks like a NAS.
traps.httpNone: No Trap IP that is on has HTTP.

exclusion.title: Vedette's own scanner does not count as a trap hit
exclusion.description: When Vedette scans for vulnerabilities or inventories actively, the box knocks on every port, traps included. To avoid false alarms, connections from the box are always ignored.
exclusion.whyBody: This is your own scanner. Without the exclusion every scan would raise a false alert.

hits.title: Trap hits
hits.description: Newest first. Includes connections to Trap IPs, honey token use and port scans across the Trap IPs. Select a time to see the hour of events around the hit.
hits.caption: Trap hits
hits.filter: Filter by service, IP or device
hits.emptyBody: Nothing has connected to a trap yet. That is good news. To see that a trap is recording, select Test trap on the Services tab.
hits.emptyBodyOff: No Trap IP is on yet, so there is nothing to record. Add one on the Trap IPs tab, then select Test trap on the Services tab to see that the trap is recording.
hits.respondLabel: Respond to the hit from {{src}} at {{time}}

hit.titleTest: Test hit on the {{service}} trap at {{time}}
hit.noDevice: This IP is not in the inventory. It may be an unknown device that just joined the network.
hit.sessionHint: Content sent by the connecting machine. Treat it as untrusted data.
hit.events: Events in the {{minutes}} minutes around the hit
hit.eventsHint: Firewall, DHCP, AD and trap events about the source machine. Rows tagged Trap come from the trap.
hit.next1: Ask the user of {{src}} whether they are browsing network folders or running a scanning tool.
hit.next2: If they do not know, unplug the machine from the network and check for unknown software and running processes.
hit.next3: Compare the firewall events after the hit: did this machine connect to any other server?
hit.meta_scan: A sweep touched the Trap IPs: {{ip}}.

device.title: Internal trap hits
device.description: Times this device connected to a trap. A normal machine has no reason to.
device.none: This device has not hit any trap.

start.title: Get started with internal traps in three steps
start.step1: On the Trap IPs tab, add a Trap IP: an address in {{lan}} that no device uses, a name, and what it should look like.
start.step2: Check that its status says Listening.
start.step3: On the Services tab, select Test trap to make sure the trap is recording. From then on every connection to a Trap IP shows up under Hits.

lanUnknown: your LAN (add it first under Devices, Scope and sensors)

trapIp.title: Trap IPs
trapIp.description: Each Trap IP is a fake machine on {{lan}}: an address no device uses, a name, and the services it answers on. Nobody has a reason to connect to it, so every connection deserves a look.
trapIp.suggestItem_one: You have {{count}} {{type}} ({{names}}), so an attacker expects to find one.
trapIp.suggestItem_other: You have {{count}} {{type}} devices ({{names}}), so an attacker expects to find them.

form.presetHint: Fills in the services and the vendor. You can change both.
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: The host name it claims, up to 15 characters: letters, digits and hyphens. It names this Trap IP in alerts.
form.ipRequired: Enter an address for the Trap IP.
form.ipHint: Not seen by Vedette so far: {{ips}}. That is not proof they are free: before a Trap IP takes an address, the box checks the network (ARP) and stops if another device answers. Use an address outside your router's DHCP pool, or reserve it there.
form.ipHintUnchecked: No devices discovered yet, so these are only guesses: {{ips}}. Before a Trap IP takes an address, the box checks the network (ARP) and stops if another device answers. Use an address outside your router's DHCP pool, or reserve it there.
form.ipHintNone: An address in your LAN that no device uses, outside your router's DHCP pool. Before a Trap IP takes it, the box checks the network (ARP).
form.vendorHint: Its MAC address starts with {{oui}}, so a scanner guesses a {{vendor}} device.
form.vendorHintNone: It gets a random-looking local MAC address, as phones and virtual machines often have.
form.servicesHint: It answers only on these ports; every other port is closed, as on a real machine. A box has one SMB share name and one HTTP login page for all its Trap IPs: see the Services tab.

trapIp.none: No Trap IP yet. Add one on an address no device uses. Two or more Trap IPs also let Vedette spot a scan.
trapIp.smbName: Its name is the NetBIOS name of the box's SMB share.

scan.title: Scan detection
scan.body: A device that touches two or more Trap IPs within a minute raises one High alert that names the source device. Normal machines have no reason to do this. Each touch is also a hit of its own.
scan.needDecoys: Turn on two or more Trap IPs first. Detection needs at least two Trap IPs.

where.macVendor: {{mac}}, which a network scanner shows as {{vendor}}
where.macNone: Given when the box holds the address
where.openNone: Nothing while it does not listen
where.openAll: Every service the box's Trap IPs use: the host program is older and cannot keep each Trap IP to its own
where.attachedMacvlan: Its own network link {{link}} (macvlan, with its own MAC) on the box card {{parent}}, inside the honeypot's isolated network. The box's own address, routes and firewall are not touched.
where.attachedMacvlanNoParent: Its own network link {{link}} (macvlan, with its own MAC) on the box's network card, inside the honeypot's isolated network. The box's own address, routes and firewall are not touched.
where.deviceLink: {{name}} has this address: the Trap IP cannot listen until one of them moves

token.title: Honey tokens
token.description: Bait you plant on real systems. Nobody has a reason to use it, so any use is an alert that names where it came from. Plant a few in places an intruder would look.

what.file: A .docx or .xlsx for a file share. It calls home when opened.
what.credential: A user and password for a password manager or a script. Any login attempt with them alerts.
what.url: A web link. Opening it alerts.
what.dns: A hostname. It cannot alert yet: the box does not answer DNS lookups, so nothing records a lookup of this name.

nameHint.credential: Looks like an old service account: svc-backup-old.
nameHint.url: Names this token in alerts, for example Wiki admin link.
nameHint.dns: Names this token in alerts, for example Backup script host.

plantHint.credential: For example the IT password manager
plantHint.url: For example an intranet wiki page
plantHint.dns: For example a backup script config

token.emptyBody: Create one above, then plant it where an intruder would look first.

trigger.file: someone opens the file in Word or Excel and it loads a hidden image from the box.
trigger.credential: anyone tries to sign in with this user name, from any machine.
trigger.url: anyone opens the link in a browser or a link scanner fetches it.
trigger.dns: nothing yet. The box does not answer DNS lookups, so this name cannot alert, even if your DNS server forwards vedette.internal to the box. Use a URL token or fake credentials for an alert you can count on.

how.file: Download {{value}} from this page and copy it to the share. In this preview there is no download: the real box generates the file with its call-home address inside, and you copy it to the share like any other document.
how.credential: Save the user and password as an entry in a password manager or a script config. Do not create the account in Active Directory: the box alerts on the failed login.
how.url: Paste the link into a wiki page, a document or a note where an intruder reads about admin systems. Whoever opens it sees a plain "404 page not found", like a dead link, and the box records who opened it.
how.dns: Do not plant {{value}} yet: a DNS token needs a DNS server on the box that answers the vedette.internal zone, and the box has none yet. Delete this token and use a URL token instead.

notHere.title: Traps need the appliance install
notHere.body: This is a container-only install: there is no vedette-host to run the honeypot container and its Trap IPs, so no trap can listen here and nothing on this page would be covered. Use the appliance install to run traps.
notHere.modules: Turn the module off in Settings, Modules

coverage.title: Is this enough?
coverage.description: A guide to which common attacker moves traps and tokens can see. It is not a score.
coverage.notListening: No Trap IP is listening yet, so the traps and tokens see none of these moves. Add a Trap IP and check that its status says Listening.

lateral.how: Trap IPs with SMB and decoy files on shares catch someone browsing for data.

credentials.how: Fake credentials alert on any login attempt. Real accounts that were stolen are not seen.

scanning.how: A sweep across the Trap IPs raises one alert that names the source.

documents.how: Decoy files and URL tokens alert when opened.

outbound.how: Not a trap job: the Logs page matches SPAN metadata and syslog against the threat lists.
outbound.howNoSpan: Not a trap job: the Logs page matches syslog against the threat lists.

endpoint.move: Malware or tools running on a computer
endpoint.how: Traps do not watch what happens on endpoints. Use endpoint protection for that.

email.how: Traps and tokens do not see email. Use your mail provider's protection.

coverage.note: Traps catch an intruder who is already inside and touches something. They do not stop a break-in. More varied bait in more places gives better odds.
